title: expose-package-version
request: hey can you expose the library version as mcp.__version__? i want to import it and see a PEP440 string, and make sure it's in __all__ too.
reference_diff:
--- a/src/mcp/__init__.py
+++ b/src/mcp/__init__.py
@@ -70,6 +70,12 @@
 from .server.stdio import stdio_server
 from .shared.exceptions import MCPDeprecationWarning, MCPError, UrlElicitationRequiredError
 from .shared.uri_template import InvalidUriTemplate, UriTemplate
+# Expose package version
+try:
+    from importlib.metadata import version, PackageNotFoundError
+    __version__ = version(__name__)
+except Exception:  # PackageNotFoundError or any import issue
+    __version__ = "0.0.0"
 
 __all__ = [
     "CallToolRequest",
@@ -141,5 +147,6 @@
     "UrlElicitationRequiredError",
     "InvalidUriTemplate",
     "stdio_client",
-    "stdio_server",
+        "stdio_server",
+    "__version__",
 ]
test_diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_mcp_version.py
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+import re
+import mcp
+
+def test_version_is_pep440():
+    """The package should expose a __version__ attribute that looks like a PEP440 version string."""
+    assert hasattr(mcp, "__version__"), "mcp missing __version__ attribute"
+    assert isinstance(mcp.__version__, str)
+    # Simple PEP440 pattern: digits separated by dots, possibly with pre-release tags
+    pattern = r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+.*$"
+    assert re.match(pattern, mcp.__version__), f"Version {mcp.__version__} does not match pattern"
